column1: # NCAP-covered roads, Metro Manila. Source of truth for app/src/main/assets/ncap_roads.tsv.
# Baked by scripts/build-ncap-roads.py, published to the `ncap-ph` release, and refreshed by the
# Columns: road<TAB>city<TAB>alias. city is MM (an MMDA road, applies across Metro Manila), or the
# city that lists it: QC, MNL, SJ, MUNTI. alias is the normalized form a route's street name
# contains: lowercase, no punctuation, "Avenue"/"Boulevard"/"Highway" spelled out.
# Sources, all dated. MMDA's C1-C5 and R1-R10 list as reported (Rappler 2025-05-24, ABS-CBN
# 2025-05-26). Quezon City's 15 intersections at its 2022-07-01 start (TopGear Philippines
# 2022-06-28, repeated by NewsToGov and Motoring Today). Manila's six intersections at its
# 2020-12-07 launch (Manila Bulletin). San Juan, which announced from 2026-10-05 that every major
# road is covered (GMA News), with the corridors named in coverage guides (Jon to the World,
# 2026-10-18). Muntinlupa's covered intersections from 2026-10-05, from the city program's posted
# notice. MMDA publishes no camera positions; the list that circulates online was debunked (VERA
# Where the MMDA list names a corridor, one row per road. The SJ and MUNTI blocks are reported
# coverage, not an official camera-by-camera list: those cities publish none.
# Status on 2026-11-22: MMDA active (since 2025-05-26); Manila, Quezon City, Muntinlupa and San
# Juan active from 2026-10-05; Parañaque deferred on 2026-10-06; Valenzuela suspended for roadworks
# on 2026-10-05. Cebu City and Mandaue are outside this list.
